title: Bridging the Financial Literacy Gap: A Digital Financial Literacy Program for Young Adults
authors: Blancaflor, S.A.; Bocaros, M.V.; Calibayan, T.M.; Camille, L.B.
venue: International Journal of Management Research and Enterprise Development
tldr: A digital financial literacy program using mobile applications and gamification significantly improves financial knowledge among young adults in the Philippines.
problem_and_motivation: Young adults in the Philippines exhibit low financial literacy rates, with 64% lacking understanding of basic financial concepts. Traditional financial education methods are often inaccessible or unengaging for digital-native generations. The gap between financial knowledge and practical application persists despite existing literacy programs.
approach: Developed a digital financial literacy program targeting young adults aged 18-30.
Created mobile-first educational modules covering budgeting, saving, investing, and debt management.
Incorporated gamification elements including challenges, quizzes, and achievement badges.
Conducted pre-test and post-test assessments with 200 participants.
Used statistical analysis to measure knowledge improvement across demographic groups.
Compared digital program effectiveness against traditional workshop-based approaches.
findings: num: 32% improvement in financial knowledge scores from pre-test to post-test.
num: 78% of participants reported increased confidence in financial decision-making.
num: 85% engagement rate with gamified modules.
num: 40% higher retention compared to traditional methods.
num: 64% of participants initially lacked understanding of basic financial concepts.
The digital format significantly outperformed traditional workshops in engagement and knowledge retention.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper demonstrates that digital-first financial literacy programs with gamification significantly outperform traditional methods in engaging young adults. The 32% knowledge improvement and 85% engagement rate validate the approach. The study provides a scalable model for addressing financial literacy gaps in developing countries through technology-enabled education.
directly_justifies: Digital financial literacy programs achieve higher engagement and retention than traditional methods.
Gamification elements significantly improve learning outcomes in financial education.
Targeted digital interventions can effectively address financial literacy gaps among young adults.
limits: Limited to 200 participants in the Philippines; generalizability to other contexts is uncertain.
Short-term knowledge measurement; long-term behavior change not assessed.
Self-reported confidence improvements may not translate to actual behavioral changes.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 1 (Current Personal Finance Landscape) is relevant through 1.A (Current State of Personal Finance Management) describing the literacy gap. Domain 3 (Psychology) partially applies through 1.D (Behavioral Barriers). Domain 12 (Evaluation Frameworks) is highly relevant through 12.A (Financial Literacy and System Evaluation) and 12.B (User Satisfaction and Adoption). Other domains like 4-11, 13, 14 are less directly applicable as the paper focuses on education rather than technical system implementation.

limitations: Sample of 200 participants limits statistical power for subgroup analyses.
Short-term assessment only; does not measure long-term financial behavior change.
Philippines-specific context may limit generalizability to other countries.
Self-reported engagement and confidence measures may introduce social desirability bias.
